A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it in scrambled form, so people on the same Wi-Fi or your internet provider can't read it.

The tunnel ends at a VPN company's computer, which then talks to websites for you. Websites see that computer's address instead of yours, so your location looks different too.

It hides your traffic from the network you're on, but the VPN company can still see it, so pick one you trust.
